one_liner: Rust GPU video denoiser (NLMeans, NLMeans-HQ, NL4D on CubeCL); first-party chart shows about 11x FFmpeg nlmeans_opencl at 1080p.
what_it_does: Denoises 8, 10 and 12-bit YUV video on the GPU with three algorithms: NLMeans (a fixed-weight `fast` variant or an `hq` variant that measures noise per scene, temporal radius 0-8), NLMeans-HQ, and NL4D, a block-matching grouped filter with motion tracking that the docs place as a cousin of V-BM3D. It ships as a CLI (input through FFMS2 or a y4m pipe, split by scene, y4m on stdout), a Rust crate (Denoiser::create, then push_frame/push_frame_wire and recv_frame/flush), and a VapourSynth plugin (vsavd on PyPI). It is not an FFmpeg filter: in an FFmpeg pipeline you pipe y4m through a separate process, and a `--preset` ladder (veryfast to veryslow) picks the variant, temporal radius and search radius.
how_it_is_fast: In the spatial pass one fused kernel launch covers the whole search window: patch distance, weight exp(-max(d - noise_offset, 0) * h2_inv_norm) and accumulation, all in f32 out of a 32x8 shared-memory tile with a halo. CubeCL compiles that kernel at runtime with the search window unrolled ((2r+1)^2 iterations, per the Denoiser::create docs), and the weight's symmetry (pixel p against p+q equals p+q against p) lets each offset's distance serve both pixels. Two scene-parallel workers and two in-flight readbacks keep the GPU busy. The baseline is weak by comparison, derived from FFmpeg's vf_nlmeans_opencl.c and nlmeans.cl: for each group of 4 offsets per plane it launches a horizontal prefix-sum kernel with one work-item per row scanning the row serially, a vertical one with one work-item per column, and a weight-accumulate kernel. That is 56 groups x 3 planes, about 500 kernel launches per frame at its defaults, followed by a clFinish on every frame.
when_to_use: Cleaning video before an encode on a machine with a GPU, where FFmpeg's nlmeans_opencl, CPU nlmeans or hqdn3d is the throughput bottleneck; the first-party 1080p 8-bit chart shows about 105-116 fps for the NLMeans arms on an AMD GPU named RX9700.
10 or 12-bit sources: depth is detected and kept, while FFmpeg's nlmeans_opencl rejects the 10-bit formats its hwupload path offers (per the benchmark config).
Temporal denoising with motion compensation and automatic per-scene noise estimation (NLMeans-HQ, NL4D), where you would otherwise hand-tune sigma per source in KNLMeansCL or run V-BM3D.
Cross-vendor GPU fleets: the same build runs on AMD, Intel and NVIDIA through Vulkan and on Apple Silicon through Metal, with no ROCm or CUDA SDK needed on the vulkan backend.
Rust programs that want an embeddable GPU denoiser with a push/receive frame API.
when_not_to_use: Machines without a usable GPU: there is no software backend (CubeCL's CPU runtime lacks the atomics the collaborative filter needs); a lavapipe-style software Vulkan device is the only CPU fallback.
C or C++ code, or an FFmpeg filter graph: there is no C API and no libavfilter filter, so integration means a separate process and a y4m pipe.

Output that must match FFmpeg's nlmeans: the 'matched' arm is not equivalent. av-denoise weights exp(-SSD/(3 s^2 x 49)) over a 7x7 patch while nlmeans_opencl uses exp(-SSD/(10s)^2) over the 6x6 window its integral-image corners cover (derived from both sources), and no PSNR or SSIM comparison is published.
Search windows wider than radius 8 (17x17) or patches wider than radius 16 (MAX_SEARCH_RADIUS, MAX_PATCH_RADIUS); FFmpeg's r goes up to 99.

Speed-critical VapourSynth graphs: through the plugin NLMeans-HQ drops from about 105 fps (CLI) to about 35 fps and NL4D from about 80 to about 29 fps at 1080p (chart readings), where NL4D only ties V-BM3D FAST (about 28 fps). It is also an alpha (0.5.0-alpha3, 14 stars, one maintainer) that has shipped backend bugs: green output and crashes on CUDA on an RTX 4080 under Windows (#13), and a motion-compensation alignment error unless frame height was a multiple of 512 (#4), both closed.

integration.form: crate (av-denoise on crates.io: library plus the CLI behind the `binary` feature; av-denoise-core holds the kernels), VapourSynth plugin wheel vsavd on PyPI, GHCR container images per backend
integration.dependencies: cubecl 0.10 (GPU JIT) with one backend feature: vulkan (default), metal, cuda (needs CUDA headers and nvcc at runtime) or rocm (needs the HIP compiler and headers at runtime); the CLI needs FFMS2 and FFmpeg libraries (optional static build via vcpkg, `static-ffms2`); anyhow, thiserror, tracing, bon, strum, etcetera
integration.min_toolchain: Rust edition 2024 (Rust 1.85+); no rust-version declared; CUDA and ROCm backends need the vendor SDK present at runtime for kernel JIT
integration.platforms: GPUs reachable through Vulkan (AMD, Intel, NVIDIA), Metal (Apple Silicon), CUDA or ROCm/HIP on Linux, macOS and Windows; published numbers cover one AMD GPU named RX9700 on the Vulkan backend
integration.thread_safety: Denoiser methods take &mut self: one stream per instance, at most MAX_PENDING = 2 readbacks in flight (more would reuse an output handle and corrupt frames, per the source). Parallelism comes from scene workers, each with its own denoiser; CubeCL runs codegen on its own per-device thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — `av-denoise nlmeans --preset veryfast --strength 1.0 --patch-radius 3 --search-radius 7` runs the same spatial NLMeans geometry as nlmeans_opencl's defaults, but as a y4m-in/y4m-out process rather than an FFmpeg filter, and with a different strength normalisation

gotchas: The first run JIT-compiles the kernels (about 10 s) and caches them on disk under a hash of the kernel source; set AV_DENOISE_COMPILATION_CACHE=off to measure the cold cost. The bundled e2e benchmark runs an untimed warm-up and leaves the cache on, so its timed pass excludes compilation, although the config comment says shader compilation counts.

When embedding: the windowed NLM kernels unroll (2 x search_radius + 1)^2 times, and a search radius of about 5 or more can overflow the 2 MiB stack of CubeCL's codegen thread and abort the process. Call raise_codegen_stack_limit() at the top of main; the workspace sets RUST_MIN_STACK to 16 MiB for cargo runs.

--strength is an absolute FFmpeg-style value only in the `fast` variant (preset veryfast). Every other preset picks `hq`, where it multiplies the measured noise level, and the default preset `base` also sets temporal radius 2, search radius 2 and patch radius 4, so the default run is not FFmpeg's geometry.

The README's '~2x FFmpeg nlmeans_opencl' and '~1.3x V-BM3D' lines disagree with its own charts (about 11x and about 1.04x like-for-like through VapourSynth). The charts were committed 2026-09-06, the day 0.4.0 was released, and have not been re-run on later code.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other denoiser is catalogued in video-audio; the siblings are codecs, resamplers, RTP stacks and a VAD. av-denoise belongs before an encoder such as SVT-AV1, x265 or VVenC as a pre-encode cleanup step. The comparisons that would matter, KNLMeansCL (which the README names as its inspiration) and the BM3DCUDA/HIP filters, are not catalogued or benchmarked here.
verified_claims_summary: One end-to-end run per arm (repeats = 1 after a warm-up; fps = probed frame count / wall time) on an unpublished 1080p 8-bit clip with an AMD GPU named RX9700. The chart shows av-denoise NLMeans at FFmpeg-matched geometry at about 116 fps against FFmpeg nlmeans_opencl at about 10.6 fps (about 11x, read from the chart), while the README text says about 2x; host CPU, FFmpeg version, driver and rustc are not published. Part of the gap comes from a weak baseline (FFmpeg's serial row and column prefix sums, about 500 launches and a clFinish per frame, single filter chain against two scene workers). KNLMeansCL, the established GPU NLMeans, is not measured, and the V-BM3D claim holds only CLI-to-plugin: through the plugin on both sides NL4D is about 29 fps against V-BM3D FAST at about 28 fps at 1080p, and slower at 4K.
status_note: Active (0.5.0-alpha3 published 2026-10-03, last commit 2026-10-03, 403 crates.io downloads) and Apache-2.0, so it is copyable as a Rust crate, CLI or VapourSynth plugin. It is an alpha with a single maintainer and 14 stars, and has no C/C++ interface.
